name: Serpens
introduction: is the Serpent, held by Ophiuchus. It is the only constellation split into two separate parts: Serpens Caput, the head, and Serpens Cauda, the tail, on either side of Ophiuchus.

sections.title: What makes it special
paragraphs: Serpens Cauda contains the Eagle Nebula, M16, home of the Pillars of Creation, towering columns of gas and dust photographed by Hubble and Webb. New stars are forming inside them.

sections.title: Notable stars
paragraphs: [Unukalhai](hip:77070), the serpent’s heart, is an orange giant 74 light-years away. [Gamma Serpentis](hip:78072), 37 light-years away, is a Sun-like star, and [Eta Serpentis](hip:89962) an orange subgiant.
[Chow](hip:77233) and [Theta¹ Serpentis](hip:92946), in the tail, are white stars.

sections.title: Beyond the stars
paragraphs: Serpens also contains the globular cluster M5, one of the oldest known, Hoag’s Object, a nearly perfect ring galaxy, and Seyfert’s Sextet, a compact group of galaxies.
